episodes.186653: A strong surface low deepened across the eastern Gulf of Mexico as high pressure dominated northeast of the region creating very strong onshore flow. Several days of persistent onshore flow increased water levels along the local Atlantic coast and within inland estuaries including the St. Johns River basin. As the low crossed the state, strong winds, heavy rainfall and storm surge impacted NE Florida and SE Georgia Saturday night 12/16 into Sunday 12/17. Wind gusts increased to 40-50 mph overnight and continued to remain strong into Sunday afternoon with gusts increasing to 45-56 mph as the low departed NE of the region with strong post-frontal pressure rises and drier air enabling strong low-level winds to mix down to the surface.
episodes.186747: A strong South Pacific Convergence Zone moved over American Samoa on December 14th through the 16th. The total rainfall from the 14th through the 16th was 10.82 inches at WSO Pago Pago, which includes 4.18 inches of rain between midnight and 3 AM on the 14th and 3.93 inches of rain fell between 1 AM and 7 AM on the 16th.  Rainfall caused numerous landslides and widespread flooding across the territory. Also, strong wind gusts were recorded from heavy rainfall and thunderstorms. The Governor of American Samoa declared a state of emergency from this event.

events.narrative: A mesonet station about 5 miles SW of the Ocala Airport measured daily storm total rainfall of 6.54 inches as of 5:45 am.
A mesonet site about 6 miles WNW of the University of Florida measured daily storm total rainfall of 5.51 inches since midnight.
A mesonet site about 2 miles WNW of Alachua measured 5.40 inches of storm total rainfall since midnight.
A mesonet site about 7 miles south of the Ocala Airport measured 5.20 inches of storm total rainfall since midnight.
An observer measured storm total rainfall of 4 inches in 24 hours about 2 miles SSE of Summerfield.
One day 24 hr rainfall total was 5.38 inches in Flagler Beach.

Storm total rainfall ranged from 3.5 to 6.25 inches across Flagler county from 12/16 through 12/17. Some of the highest values were 6.25 inches measured in the F section of Palm Coast, 5.47 inches in Flagler Beach, 4.98 inches in Plantation Bay, and 4.45 inches at the Flagler County EOC in Bunnell.
Emergency management reported a landslide in the village of Poloa on the morning of the 16th. Nobody was injured. The exact time of the landslide is unknown.
With gusts reaching around 46 MPH (40 knots), large boxes that were decorated for Christmas fell to the ground and damaged the decorations.
Emergency Management reported a landslide in the village of Aoa on the morning of the 16th. Nobody was injured. The exact timing of the landslide is unknown.
Due to heavy rainfall, a stream overflowed to bring small rocks and other debris to cover the main roadway.
Emergency Management reported major flooding on Fagaima Road due to poor water drainage in the area.
Storm total rainfall in 24 hours was 5.42 inches in Nocatee.
